# **Software Development Plan** 

# 

1. # **Introduction** {#introduction}

This Software Development Plan defines the scope, team responsibilities, five-sprint schedule, software builds, and progress reporting for PhysiX. It guides the Phy6 team through the Inception, Elaboration, and Construction phases of the CS300 project.

2. # **Project Overview**

   1. ## **Project Purpose, Scope, and Objectives** {#project-purpose,-scope,-and-objectives}

Purpose: Develop PhysiX, a web-based 3D physics laboratory that helps secondary-school students in Grades 6–12 understand physics through experiments and measurements. Teachers can use it for classroom demonstrations.  
Scope: The project will focus on delivering a core set of features for students and teachers. The main functionalities will include:

* A Curriculum Experiment Library with ready-to-launch experiments.  
* An Open Laboratory for free exploration and apparatus assembly.  
* Interactive 3D simulations for an initial selection of physics experiments. Simple Pendulum and Projectile Motion are the initial candidates.  
* Experiment controls (start, pause, reset, parameter adjustment).  
* Virtual measuring tools and dynamic results/graphs plotting.  
* An optional AI-driven contextual assistant for guidance.  
* The initial scope will not include a native mobile application, multiplayer collaboration, or user account management.

Objectives: By the end of the project, we aim to achieve the following objectives:

* Deliver a deployed, working web application with all the features defined in the scope.  
* Implement the selected experiments with consistent physics calculations, virtual instrument readings, and result graphs.  
* Ensure the platform is user-friendly and provides clear, understandable measurements and visual feedback to students.

  2. ##  **Assumptions and Constraints**

Assumptions:

* The 5-person team can complete the defined scope within the 5-sprint schedule, leveraging free or education-tier development tools.  
* A functional 3D rendering engine (e.g., Three.js/Babylon.js) can be successfully integrated with React on the frontend.  
* Analytical formulas for the selected experiments are available and verifiable against standard physics textbooks.

Constraints:

* Schedule: The project has a fixed, non-negotiable 10-week (5-sprint) deadline (October–December 2026).  
* Team: The project team is fixed at 5 members with limited time alongside other coursework.  
* Environment: Desktop/laptop web browsers with WebGL support are the primary target; mobile 3D optimization is excluded.  
* Budget: This is a zero-budget project. All tools, assets, and hosting must be from free-tier plans.

3. # **Project Organization** {#project-organization}

   1. ## **Organizational Structure** {#organizational-structure}

Phy6 consists of five members led by the Project Manager, who also performs business analysis. The Software Architect defines the technical structure. Frontend and backend developers implement the application, while two members share testing responsibilities. The instructor and teaching assistants review deliverables and provide feedback.  
Members collaborate across requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, and documentation. Each work item has one responsible owner and a reviewer. The Project Manager coordinates release approval; work completed by the manager is reviewed by another team member.

4. # **Management Process** {#management-process}

   1. ## **Project Estimates** {#project-estimates}

   2. ## **Project Plan** {#project-plan}

      1. ### Phase and Iteration Plan {#phase-and-iteration-plan}

| Phase / sprint | Dates in 2026 | Objectives and exit criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Inception / S1 | 05–18 Oct | Agree on the two-mode product direction, consolidate available user evidence, prepare Vision/SDP and 3–6 UI sketches, produce two weekly reports, and establish assigned tracking tasks. |
| Elaboration / S2 | 19 Oct–01 Nov | Confirm the initial experiment/apparatus subset; refine use cases; test equipment discovery, placement, supported setup validation and reset; record technical choices and revised estimates. |
| Elaboration / S3 | 02–15 Nov | Produce architecture and a working first experiment: open a prepared experiment, interact with supported apparatus in Open Lab, run/pause/reset, and check initial measurements against references. |
| Construction / S4 | 16–29 Nov | Complete the agreed experiment subset across the two modes; integrate instruments, data and graphs; refine UI and execute integration tests. Add optional AI only if core work is stable. |
| Construction / S5 | 30 Nov–13 Dec | Run regression, browser, usability and performance checks; fix blocking defects; finalize documentation and demonstrate the tested build. |

   At sprint planning, the team selects tasks, assigns owners, identifies dependencies, and defines acceptance criteria. At sprint review, members demonstrate completed work and record outstanding defects. A retrospective identifies improvements for the next sprint.

      2. ### Releases

   

| Build / target | Type | Planned content and testing |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Build 1 / 15 Nov | Internal demo | One selected experiment with prepared setup, a limited Open Lab apparatus set, simulation controls, initial instruments, and physics reference tests. |
| Build 2 / 29 Nov | Integrated demo | Integrated guided and open-laboratory workflows for the selected experiments, with apparatus interaction, measurements, and results. Test experiment switching, reset, and data consistency. |
| Build 3 / 13 Dec | Final demo | A stable application with regression, compatibility, usability, and performance results; deployment/run instructions and user guidance. Verify AI failure handling if AI support is included. |

   Three software builds will be produced for testing. A technical prototype in Sprint 2 will evaluate apparatus interaction and rendering feasibility. Changes are tested and reviewed before integration into a release build.

3. ## **Project Monitoring and Control** {#project-monitoring-and-control}

   1. ### Reporting {#reporting}

Project progress and team communication will be managed through the following channels:  
\- Messenger: Send team announcements, communicate urgent changes, and hold quick discussions.

\- Slack: Send task reminders, follow up on deadlines, and remind members to update their progress.

\- Jira: Assign tasks, identify responsible members, schedule work by sprint, and track task status. Members update their tasks and link completed work to documents, code changes, or test results.

\- Weekly reports: Summarize completed work, ongoing tasks, blockers, and next steps. The Project Manager consolidates the report. PA1 includes two reports for the two weeks of Inception.

\- Meetings and minutes: Review progress and resolve blockers during weekly meetings. Store decisions, assigned actions, and deadlines in the shared Google Drive folder.

2. ### Risk Management 

   3. ### Configuration Management {#configuration-management}

Source code: GitHub stores application code, physics models, configuration, and technical documentation. Members develop on task branches and submit pull requests for review before merging into the main branch. Release tags identify packaged builds.

Documents and assets: A shared Google Drive workspace stores plans, reports, meeting records, UI designs, and submission files. Revision histories identify document changes. Jira tasks link to the relevant source changes and deliverables.

Configuration and change control: Environment variables and protected server configuration store credentials. Dependency versions and third-party asset licenses are recorded. Changes to scope or requirements are reviewed for schedule and implementation impact, then reflected in the affected documents and Jira tasks.
